verdict.rationale: Cua documents isolated environments for agents: the SDK creates computers on Docker/Podman (with gVisor when installed), QEMU, or Lume VMs. Its docs describe starting coding agents 'inside a Space or sandbox', and a community user reports sandboxing Claude in a Lume VM. However, no evidence says these environments are kept away from production data or credentials, and moving signed-in apps into a Space suggests real accounts can be reached. A user's request for an ephemeral one-shot VM mode suggests disposable throwaway test environments are not documented. missing for 10: documented separation from production data and credentials, ephemeral/disposable sandbox mode, explicit test-vs-production environment guidance.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: the SDK uses Docker or Podman (gVisor when installed), QEMU, or Lume on Apple silicon. Any OCI image works.
Start Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents inside a Space or sandbox
Lume: macOS and Linux VMs on Apple silicon.
